rows.abstract: The proposed MARITIME AND OCEAN AFFAIRS CENTER shall, among others: (1) Promote the development of national capabilities and institutions, including human resources, for maritime and ocean affairs; (2) Initiate steps to harmonize and/or update domestic legislation and rules and regulations with international agreements or non-binding instruments to which the Philippines is a party; (3) Create and maintain a central database on maritime and ocean affairs; and (4) Embark on activities necessary to raise the natinal archipelagic consciousness, and communicate and publicize in a coordinated manner, national maritime and ocean interests and issues.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING A PERIOD ENDING DECEMBER 31, 2010 OF FILING APPLICATIONS FOR ADMINISTRATIVE LEGALIZATION (FREE PATENT) AND JUDICIAL CONFIRMATION OF IMPERFECT AND INCOMPLETE TITLES TO ALIENABLE AND DISPOSABLE LANDS OF THE PUBLIC DOMAIN UNDER CHAPTERVII AND CHAPTER VIII OF COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 141, AS AMENDED, COMMENCING JANUARY 1, 2001
rows.abstract: Rationale: Free patent is the most affordable means by which a legitimate claimant can acquire a title over the land he is lawfully occupying. This is different from the other mode of titling which is through judicial proceedings where the private individual has to undergo the rigors of court proceedings and has to contend with the litigation expenses that usually accompany this mode of land titling.> Statistics shows that there are still 65 municipalities that have not been cadastrally surveyed while 368 are on-going and have not been completed. It will be disservice to our citizen if they will not be given the opportunity to file free patent application just because the period has not been extended.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04628

rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to give ample protection to government officials and employees who, in the diligent performance of their duties and responsibilitie s, are exposed to all hazards and harassment. > Pursuant to the above declared policy,retiring or resigning government officials and employees with administative, criminal or civil cases who eventually are exonerated or cleared therefrom shall receive their retirement or separation pay and benefits with added compounded interest for that period from their retirement or separation date to the date of the promulgation of the decision on their cases.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE PROCEDURE IN THE SEIZURE AND CONFISCATION OF PROHIBITED DRUGS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 36 OF THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT
rows.abstract: Rationale: The rise in drug incidence is a result of rampant drug peddling due to the seemingly inadequate provisions and inappropriate sanctions under existing laws. As a consequence, drug proliferates in the market. In the face of this growing drug menace, the only logical choice is to adopt a stronger policy on drugs if we are to preserve law and order and promote peace in our society.> This bill prescribes the PROCEDURE in the CUSTODY of seized prohibited and regulated drugs. It, likewise,mandates the IMMEDIATE DISPOSITION OR DESTRUCTION THEREOF.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE WALING-WALING AS THE NATIONAL FLOWER OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Sampaguita was designated as the Philippines National flower by virtue of Executive Proclamation No. 652 issued by Gov. Gen. Frank Murphy on February 1, 1934. > According to Dr. Eduardo Quisumbing National Museum Director, and Dr. Vicente Saplala, a professor of the UP Los Banos, the sampaguita is a native of India and Arabia while the Walingwaling "is not only indigenous but endemic to the Philippines." > Aside from having its origin in the Philippines, the Waling-waling floweris truly symbolic of the Filipino traits and characteristics .

rows.abstract: SECTION 1. Section 367 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, is hereby amended to read as follows: "SEC. 367. Procurement through Personal Canvass. - [Upon approval by the Committee on Awards] [p]Procurementof supplies may be affected after personal canvass of at least three (3) responsible suppliers in the locality by a committee of three (3) composed of the local general services officer or the municipal barangay treasurer, as the case may be, the local accountant, and the head of office or department for whose use the supplies are being procured. rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2001 REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to make a COMPREHENSIVE AMENDMENT to RA No. 6425, the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972. Salient amendments deal on the following: (1) Increased membership in the Dangerous Drugs Board; (2) Single definition of "DANGEROUS SRUGS", and "DANGEROUS DRUGS PREPARATION"; (3) Increased penalties and fines; (4) Requirement of mandatory drug testing for applicants of driver's license, permit to carry firearms, employment; and entry into the military service.

rows.abstract: "Home Development Mutual Fund Law of 2001". Rationale: The Legislature should take a pro-active and enactive stance to make Pag-IBIG Fund a more revitalized social institution. For example, Pag-IBIG Fund should be able to deal directly with possiblefunders, both foreign and domestic, without going through intermediaries, since the cost of having intermediaries would just add to the cost of funds. It should be able to go after erring employers, both private and government, who always resort toevery measure possible just for them not to give the employer counterpart contributions. rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE REFUSAL OF FUNERAL PARLORS AND MORGUES TO RELEASE THE REMAINS OF A DECEASED FOR BURIAL, CREMATION AND OTHER APPROPRIATE RITUALS DUE TO MONETARY REASONS
rows.abstract: "The Burial Right Act of 2001". In all cases, it shall be lawful for any proprietor, president, director, manager or any other officer or employee of a funeral parlot or morgue to refuse, disallow, or to cause the disallowance of the release of theremains of a deceased intended to be buried, cremated, or to be disposed in an appropriate ritual because of reasons pertaining to monetary commitments. It shall also be unlawful to request, solicit, demand, or accept any deposit any other form of advance payment has a prerequisite for the acceptance of the remains in such funeral parlot or morgues.
